questions.text: A mechanism or technology used in Ethernet by which two connected devices choose common transmission parameters such as speed, duplex mode and flow control is called
questions.solution:
Ethernet auto-negotiation lets two connected devices agree on speed, duplex mode and flow control automatically.

Answer: Auto negotiation

questions.text: Suppose you are browsing the world wide web using a web browser and trying to access the web servers. What is the underlying protocol and port number that are being used?
questions.solution:
HTTP runs over TCP on port 80. (Port 25 is SMTP.)

Answer: TCP, 80

questions.text:
Assume the following information.
Original timestamp value = 46
Receive timestamp value = 59
Transmit timestamp value = 60
Timestamp at arrival of packet = 69
Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
ICMP timestamp method:
- Round trip = (69 [latex]-[/latex] 46) [latex]-[/latex] (60 [latex]-[/latex] 59) = 22 ms, one way = 11 ms
- Time difference = receive [latex]-[/latex] (original + one way) = 59 [latex]-[/latex] (46 + 11) = +2 ms

The positive value means the receiver's clock is ahead, so it must go back. Only option 1 says this. (The value 3 ms in the key comes from the textbook version of this example, where the return time is 67: 59 [latex]-[/latex] (46 + 10) = 3.)

Answer: Receive clock should go back by 3 milliseconds

Transmit and Receive clocks are synchronized

Receive clock should go ahead by 1 milliseconds

questions.text: A supernet has a first address of 205.16.32.0 and a supernet mask of 255.255.248.0. A router receives 4 packets with the following destination addresses.which packet belongs to this supernet?
questions.solution:
Mask 255.255.248.0 = /21, so third octet 32 = 00100 000 fixes the top 5 bits. The supernet covers 205.16.32.0 to 205.16.39.255.

Only 205.16.39.44 falls in this range.

Answer: 205.16.39.44

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: An IP packet has arrived with the first 8 bits as 0100 0010. Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
First 4 bits = 0100 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] version 4. Next 4 bits = 0010 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] HLEN = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] header = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 8 bytes.

The minimum IPv4 header is 20 bytes (HLEN 5), so the packet is invalid and is discarded.

Answer: The receiver rejects the packet
